Title: [Submission] Keeper of Tradition (Camarilla reward for playing Traditions)

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
Name: Keeper of Tradition
Cardtype: Action
+1 stealth action. Requires a ready prince or justicar.
Remove from your ash heap 3 different tradition cards that this vampire has played. This Camarilla vampire gets +2 bleed and +2 vote. Burn this card if this vampire changes sect.

The hard part is keeping track of who played what. Requiring to play this card first would make it much weaker.

Prince of Paris, France

Ratings Coordinator, Rules Director

Messages.Author: jamesatzephyr
Messages.Body:
> Ankha wrote:
> Name: Keeper of Tradition
> Cardtype: Action
> +1 stealth action. Requires a ready prince or justicar.
> Remove from your ash heap 3 different tradition cards that this vampire has played. This Camarilla vampire gets +2 bleed and +2 vote. Burn this card if this vampire changes sect.
>
Could you explain the game need?

Second Tradition is already excellent. Third Tradition is very good, but they can be fragile and get burned. (Also, you could probably do that yourself using, say, Fortitude as your skill card for appropriate action modifiers, if you wanted.) Playing them is their own reward. I'm not sure that decks using those cards really need 2 extra votes and 2 extra bleed by popping a couple of Fourth or Fifth Tradition in them.

First Tradition is potentially very good indeed, but needs a bit more thinking about. Such a deck could probably combine First and Second fairly easily, and then get a fairly hefty reward by bringing in a relatively easy to play Fourth or Fifth.

(Sixth Tradition is generally terrible. In most situations, you'd much rather play Carlton because he's much, much less corner case, even with his cost.)

> Ankha wrote:
> The hard part is keeping track of who played what. Requiring to play this card first would make it much weaker.
>
More problematically, Third Tradition goes in play. If you have more than one breeder, tracking which progeny is which for when they get burned could be quite cumbersome.

> Timo wrote:
> Why do you think it would be weaker ?
>
Five of the six traditions are actions, meaning that you give players a significant heads-up about which actions to block etc. If both Constanza and Donal are playing Traditions, which one of them do you block in preference? Of course, if you're having to keep track anyway, that may well give them that heads up.

Of course, forcing it to come after also makes it annoying in that you may well have it jamming your hand. You could phrase it as "Put this card on this vampire. During your discard phase, the Prince or Justicar with this card may burn it and three traditions..." or something like that, if you wanted.

Having many opportunities to block may give you more chance of blocking than just one critical action. Not all decks can summon a large amount of intercept on command, when - say - an Obfuscate-driven Prince deck holds a Lost in Crowds and a Forgotten Labyrinth for that crucial moment. Having the option of blocking that or blocking the less-likely-to-be-played-in-large-numbers Fourth or Fifth Traditions may give you a better chance of doing so. You also get the opportunity to DI the KoT or the Tradition, knowing that you've got the 'right' vampire etc.

Messages.Author: jamesatzephyr
Messages.Body:
> Ankha wrote:
> It's to encourage people to play the various tradition cards (especially 4th and 5th that are rarely played; the 6th is even rarer) by rewarding them. Who plays 5th Traditions nowadays (even though it's an okay card) ?
>
Assuming the card shakes down as being worth playing at all, I'd expect that what it's massively more likely to do is encourage people to continue to play the good tradition cards (2nd, 3rd already played a fair bit, a smattering of 1st) and include one or two others if necessary. That is, if it has any impact at all, it would be to make Camarilla Prince decks using good traditions better. And since those Camarilla Prince decks are typically already using cards like Parity Shift which are very good indeed, I'm not sure they need the help - I'm not sure that making, say, a CAmarilla breed deck with Parity Shift, Second Tradition, Third Tradition, a few Con Boons, and encouraging it to add a couple of First Traditions is actually giving Fourth and Fifth a shot in the arm, or encouraging deck diversity, or anything else. Maybe a breed-boon deck stuffed with 2nd and 3rd gets three Fifth Tradition to refill itself (e.g. Prince1 tops up Prince2 a bit), and to get more votes and more bleed - making a very, very solid deck that bit stronger.

The basic thing is: Camarilla Prince decks can already be very strong. If this is worth playing, it would make them stronger. I don't really see that being warranted.

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
> Lech wrote:
> Um, it's perfect card for nosferatu princes. Do you think it need more help?
>
Could you develop?
I suppose you're talking about Nosferatu because you have "Nosferatu royalties" archetype in mind ( Ruben's deck is a good example). Unfortunately, that kind of decks don't play that many Traditions. First, usually they focus on 2nd and 3rd tradition, meaning a third different tradition is missing. Of if they play also another tradition, the quantities are low (meaning it's unlikely to draw the 3 different traditions early in the game). And most importantly, they rely a lot on Third Tradition that doesn't go easily in the ash heap once played (someone has to burn the Progeny).

Basically, you can't just add that card in a Nosferatu Royalty deck and expect it to work. You'll have to add more traditions, more various, less focused and that's the intent.

Prince of Paris, France

Messages.Author: direwolf
Messages.Body:
Keeping track of which vampire played which card in your ash heap should NEVER be a game mechanic.

If you want a card like that (I do not condone or condemn the need for such a card  ) I would try something like:

Rules Lawyer
Master. Archetype.
Put this card on a titles Camarilla vampire. At the end of a turn in which this vampire plays a Tradition card, remove the card from the game and add a counter to this card. This vampire may burn X counters for X bleed or votes. A vampire may have only one archetype.

Independent Futurist. Contrarian (titled, X votes where X is the number of votes as the acting minion.) Target Vitals is always the better combat card.
